correctness.rationale: For the named complete r-partite base in the homogeneous K_{r+1}-free graph, one-point extension and quantifier elimination identify nonalgebraic complete singleton types with neighbor sets missing at least one shore. Thus c_1=n and Q=(1+z)^n-P_A is the product of shore factors, q_r=product(a_i). The coefficient of t^(2j) in log[Q(exp(t)-1)/(q_r t^r)] is B_(2j)/(2j(2j)!) times the 2j-th shore power sum (differentiate log(sinh(t/2)/(t/2)) to check the factor). The even Bernoulli numbers are nonzero and the coefficient needs no grade above r+2j, with absent coefficients understood as zero. The first r-1 moments of the squared sizes and their product q_r^2 determine the squared-size polynomial by Newton identities and hence the positive sizes. For three shores, direct product expansion gives q_4=q_3(n-3)/2 and 12 q_5/q_3=2n^2-12n+21-(ab+ac+bc); grades 1,3,5 therefore suffice. Independent equal-sum/product enumeration via combinations with replacement covered all 67 sorted positive triples of total size 3–13, proving no smaller collision and the unique one at 13. Direct counts give common prefix (1,13,78,250,535) and c_5=822,798. Appending r-3 unit shores shifts the difference by exactly r-3 grades. value.rationale: The graded singleton counts are a natural structural measurement of a named Henson base. Recovering all shore sizes with a bounded number of grades despite unbounded total size is a meaningful inverse theorem, and in the first nontrivial tripartite case the sharp cutoff and explicit indistinguishable pair explain exactly why the preceding grade fails. The known unary count alone would not supply that conclusion.
